To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dogfish has a BBB that is as tight as that of the rat, that a large part of the transport of materials across the dogfish BBB occurs by carrier-like processes, that the distribution of materials within the dogfish brain is virtually identical to that in the rat brain, and that the dogfish possesses a special urea transport system which facilitates the movement of this substance between blood and brain tissue.

(a) in dogfish and rat, the BBB is nearly as tight to sucrose as is that of mammalian species; (b) in both species, the tissue distribution space for water is about the same as that for inulin, and the tissue distribution space is nearly the same in the dogfish and rat; and (c) the dogfish possesses a special urea transport system which facilitates the transfer of this compound across the BBB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparative physiology of the BBB and the comparative physiology of brain water and ion homeostasis.
the comparative aspects of brain metabolism and blood-brain exchange in the dogfish and rat.
the comparative aspects of the exchange of various materials between blood, brain, and cerebro-spinal fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are more similarities than differences between the dogfish and rat in the distribution of materials from blood to brain tissue.
the dogfish brain is not significantly different in the way it handles extracellular nonelectrylytes, hexoses, and urea than the rat brain.
the BBB in dogfish is very similar to that of the rat, although there are some interesting differences which may be related to the lower blood flow of the dogfish.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dogfish brain is a very efficient organ in terms of its ability to extract and distribute materials from the circulation, and that the BBB of this animal may be more permeable than that of the rat.
, in the dogfish, the BBB appears to be a major factor in determining the distribution of material in the brain.
the dogfish is a very useful comparative model for mammalian species in the study of the BBB and the exchange of material with the CNS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dogfish may provide a useful comparative model for studies of blood-brain transfer in a species which is not nearly as expensive to maintain as the rat.

, despite the many differences between the dogfish and mammalian species, the dogfish brain appears to be remarkably similar to the mammalian brain in terms of its blood-brain exchange characteristics.
, although the dogfish is an animal with a very different physiology than mammals, the BBB and CSF system of this animal are remarkably similar in many ways to those of the rat.
